headline: Signature proposed for mac-dir-stat: a calm inventory that separates what can be rebuilt from what only you have, with honest scale beside the treemap. Awaiting Pavol's pick; nothing built.

lineage.source: Shneiderman, Tree visualization with tree-maps (ACM ToG); cushion (1999) and squarified (2000) treemaps
lineage.changes: Keep the squarified layout; add a scale key and a plain, cushion-free map mode.

lineage.source: Cleveland & McGill, Graphical Perception (JASA); replicated by Heer & Bostock (CHI 2010)
lineage.changes: Ranked length ledger beside the treemap, synced on hover, so comparisons use length, not area.

lineage.source: Tufte, The Visual Display of Quantitative Information / Envisioning Information
lineage.changes: 'Since the last scan' summary and small multiples of past scans; data-ink-only map mode.
Cleanup becomes a two-column inventory: rebuildable (selectable) vs only-yours (shown, never offered for deletion).
Each cleanup row shows the command and plain time estimate to get it back.
A short closing account after a trash action: what left, what is still recoverable, free space now.

mechanics.name: Move 1 — The inventory (1A two columns, recommended; 1B cost to get it back; 1C closing account)
mechanics.metric: Conversion rate among scan-completers and median bytes freed; guard: no data-loss reports

mechanics.name: Move 2 — Honest scale (2A ledger beside the map, recommended; 2B scale key; 2C plain map)
mechanics.metric: Time from scan done to first trash/move (key_action) falls; zoom-ins per session fall

mechanics.name: Move 3 — The disk over time (3A since the last scan, recommended; 3B small multiples; 3C nothing)
mechanics.metric: 90-day return scans per install (weekly scan-completers guard)

decisions.question: Move 1: which inventory option?
decisions.default_taken: none (recommend 1A with 1B's line under each row)
decisions.why: 1A carries the whole idea in one look and no competitor does it; nothing is built before Pavol picks.

decisions.question: Move 2: which scale option?
decisions.why: Fixes the known weakness of treemaps (area is read poorly); 2C folds into the visual signature.

decisions.question: Move 3: keep scan history?
decisions.why: Answers 'what grew?' with one stored summary and no new window.

decisions.question: Visual signature: replace the violet accent and dark-first theme with book typography on paper?
decisions.why: Matches Pavol's stated taste and moves away from the generic AI-app look.

competitors.name: DaisyDisk
competitors.note: Sunburst, collector for one-go deletion, shows purgeable/hidden space; closed source.

competitors.name: GrandPerspective
competitors.price: Free (GPL); ~$2.99 / €3 supporter price on Mac App Store
competitors.note: Treemap with colour by folder/type/age; updated in 2026; no cleanup guidance.

competitors.name: OmniDiskSweeper
competitors.note: Size-sorted column browser with delete; no visualisation; rare updates.

competitors.name: Disk Inventory X
competitors.note: Treemap plus file-type list; largely dormant.

competitors.name: macOS Storage settings
competitors.note: Category bar and recommendations; opaque 'System Data'.

competition.gap: No tool separates what can be rebuilt from what only you have, or says what deleting costs to get back. A free, open-source treemap with an honest inventory, plain claims, and AI that proposes but never approves is unoccupied.
